fair_value.method: Blend of 2027E P/E (EPS $4.30 x 8.5x = $36.5), 2027E EV/EBITDA ($780M x 5.5x less ~$250M end-2027 net debt / ~106M diluted shares = $38) and a long-term-copper NAV cross-check (~$29) that strips out today's record copper price; weights 0.40/0.35/0.25 give ~$35.5.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2027E EPS $4.30 (10% haircut to Alpha Vantage consensus $4.79, 13 analysts, range $3.59-5.89, for Ero's history of guidance cuts and copper mean reversion) x 8.5x (mid-cycle multiple for a single-country Brazilian mid-tier copper producer near peak prices)

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E EBITDA $780M (80kt Cu at ~$5.50/lb net realized, C1 ~$2.10/lb, 50-55koz Au, H1-26 run rate $269M EBITDA on ~34.6kt Cu) x 5.5x (vs 5.7x forward cited Sep-2026) = EV $4.29B; less est. end-2027 net debt ~$250M (from $453M at Q2-26 with OCF $138M/qtr and capex tapering after shaft); / ~106M diluted shares

methods.name: other (NAV at long-term copper)
methods.inputs: Operating NAV ~$3.0B for Caraiba+Tucuma+Xavantina at $4.75/lb LT copper, $3,000/oz LT gold, 8% real discount rate; plus ~$0.5B risked Furnas option (PEA 108kt CuEq/yr, PFS 2027, FID 2029, Vale 11% carry); less ~$0.45B net debt; / ~106M shares

bear.story: Copper retreats from ~$6.8/lb record toward $4.5/lb as the squeeze unwinds and macro slows; Pilar external shaft slips into 2028 and 2026 copper lands at low end of 67.5-77.5kt guidance (another miss); multiple compresses to ~6x EPS of ~$3.3.

base.story: Copper stays elevated but off peak (~$5.25-5.75/lb); 2026 guidance met, shaft commissioned during 2027, 2027 copper ~75-85kt, net debt falls toward ~$250M and capital returns begin; stock rerates little from ~8x forward EPS.

bull.story: Copper holds $6+/lb, shaft on time lifts Caraiba throughput and grade, Tucuma reaches 4Mtpa; 2027 EPS ~$5.5+, balance sheet near net cash, buyback/dividend, Furnas PFS derisks growth; ~10x EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$22 (about -42%, and below where the stock sat before the 2026 copper rally) the market would be pricing either a major operational failure (Pilar shaft delay/cost blowout, Tucuma throughput/tailings problems, another guidance cut) or a copper collapse toward ~$4/lb that removes the deleveraging story; ordinary 64%-vol noise around a ~$36 fair value should not reach it on company-neutral news.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 production release (tests second-half weighting of guidance)
Q4/FY2026 production vs 67.5-77.5kt guidance and 2027 guidance / three-year outlook
Updated Tucuma reserve report and possible shareholder-return framework
Pilar external shaft commissioning at Caraiba
End of historic gold-concentrate stockpile sales at Xavantina (revenue step-down)
Copper price path from record ~$6.8/lb Comex (Sep 2026) and BRL/USD

key_uncertainties: Copper price mean reversion from record highs; ERO earnings are highly levered to copper
Timing of the Pilar external shaft and Caraiba grade/throughput
Ero's track record of missing/lowering production guidance
Tucuma plant throughput and tailings filtration capacity
Brazilian real and Brazil country risk; FX hedge gains ($40-45M in 2026) not repeatable
Pace of deleveraging and whether capital returns begin
reasoning: ERO (Ero Copper, Brazil copper/gold) doubled in a year mainly on copper hitting records (LME 3M $14,875/t, Comex $6.83/lb Sep-2026) plus improving execution: Q1-26 17.3kt Cu, adj EPS $0.69; Q2-26 17.3kt Cu, adj EBITDA $144M, adj EPS $0.83, OCF $138M, net debt down to $453M, guidance (67.5-77.5kt Cu, C1 $2.15-2.35/lb) maintained but H2-weighted; capex raised to $285-330M; gold at low end. Three-year outlook 75-85kt (2027) and 80-90kt (2028) depends on the Pilar shaft. Consensus 2027 EPS $4.79 puts the stock at ~7.9x, cheap only if copper stays near records; analysts mixed (several downgrades in 2026, CIBC Hold, Seeking Alpha $50 Buy). My blended fair value ~$35.5 is slightly under spot because I haircut peak-copper earnings and weight a long-term-copper NAV. I model a lognormal centered around a ~$36 median with ~50% annual vol (below realized 64% as the stock is now larger and less levered, but still a single-asset-country miner), which yields ~46% chance of finishing above $38 and ~18% of being below $19, consistent with scenario weights 25/50/25 at $20/$38/$56. Research limited to web search and consensus data; CMD details were mostly paywalled.
